schema_version: 1
id: am-callout
kind: effect
pack_id: astrid_motion
short_description: Floating white callout card joined to an anchor by a stepped orange curved connector with dot end-caps.
description: The site's annotation device. A panel-white card (1px rule border, soft shadow, Gelasio heading at weight 650, Inter body) sits at x, y. An orange curved connector leaves the card's nearest side at the title line and draws in on 2-frame steps over drawFrames to a dot at the anchor. The card appears on the first frame with a cut.
keywords:
- callout
- annotation
- card
- connector
- specimen
- label
outputs:
- name: clip
  type: clip
  artifact_type: clip/visual
  description: Callout overlay.
metadata:
  label: AM Callout
  description: Floating callout card with a stepped orange connector to an anchor point.
  whenToUse: Use to annotate a thing in a plate or a UI sketch, such as a specimen label or a figure caption. Give x, y and width for the card in canvas px, and anchor for where the connector ends. The connector attaches to the card's left or right edge, depending on which side the anchor is on.
  role: "label"
  text: ["title","body"]
  summary: "{title}"
  geometry: {"position":["x","y"],"scale":null,"full_frame":false}
defaults:
  title: ''
  body: ''
  x: 1200
  y: 160
  width: 520
  anchor:
    x: 960
    y: 540
  drawFrames: 12
  stepFrames: 2
dependencies:
  js_packages: []
  python_requirements: []
schema:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: true
  properties:
    title:
      type: string
    body:
      type: string
    x:
      type: number
      description: Canvas px for the card top-left.
    y:
      type: number
      description: Canvas px for the card top-left.
    width:
      type: number
      exclusiveMinimum: 0
      description: Canvas px.
    anchor:
      type: object
      description: Canvas px where the connector ends.
      properties:
        x:
          type: number
        y:
          type: number
    drawFrames:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      description: Frames for the connector to finish drawing.
    stepFrames:
      type: integer
      enum:
      - 2
      - 3
    titleSize:
      type: number
      description: Title size in canvas px (default 40).
    bodySize:
      type: number
      description: Body size in canvas px (default 24). Use 32+ for text that must read at review size.

schema_version: 1
id: am-churn
kind: effect
pack_id: astrid_motion
short_description: "Ledger of obsession: real git totals count up on a timeline, commits stamp in, a heartbeat grows."
description: "Full-frame data passage. A split-flap date readout and a timeline track sit top. LINES WRITTEN (ink, orange ticks) and LINES DELETED (rust) count the cumulative daily totals and end exactly on params.totals. Real commits stamp into a column on their day, oldest scrolling out in 6 px steps. A heartbeat draws added up and deleted down. timeline sets the date per frame; freezeAt spotlights a commit."
keywords:
  - ledger
  - churn
  - git
  - counter
  - commits
  - heartbeat
  - timeline
  - data
outputs:
  - name: clip
    type: clip
    artifact_type: clip/visual
    description: Full-frame ledger overlay.
metadata:
  label: AM Churn Ledger
  description: Data-driven ledger of commits, counters and heartbeat, driven by a date timeline.
  whenToUse: Use for the churn passage with real repository totals. Pass rows (one per day, contiguous, hand-ish counts), highlights (about 40 real commits), totals (which must equal the row sums), and a timeline of {atFrame, date} keys that ends on endDate. Use variant dark for night frames.
  role: "card"
  summary: "Git ledger from {startDate} to {endDate}"
  geometry: {"position":["x","y"],"scale":"width","full_frame":false}
dependencies:
  js_packages: []
  python_requirements: []
defaults:
  rows: []
  highlights: []
  totals: {commits: 0, added: 0, deleted: 0}
  startDate: ""
  endDate: ""
  timeline: []
  freezeAt: null
  footnote: ""
  variant: paper
  layout: full
  width: 1920
  height: 1080
  x: 0
  y: 0
  binDays: 11
  scrollFrames: 14
schema:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: true
  required: [rows, totals]
  properties:
    rows:
      type: array
      description: One entry per calendar day from startDate to endDate, ascending, zero-filled. added and deleted are the hand-ish daily counts; commits is optional.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [date, added, deleted]
        properties:
          date: {type: string, description: "ISO date, YYYY-MM-DD."}
          commits: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          added: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          deleted: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    highlights:
      type: array
      description: Real commits to stamp in, chronological. subject is the real commit subject.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [date, repo, sha, subject]
        properties:
          date: {type: string}
          repo: {type: string}
          sha: {type: string}
          subject: {type: string}
          added: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          deleted: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    totals:
      type: object
      required: [commits, added, deleted]
      description: Exact totals; the last row's cumulative values are forced to these at endDate.
      properties:
        commits: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
        added: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
        deleted: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    startDate: {type: string, description: "ISO date of rows[0]. Informational."}
    endDate: {type: string, description: "ISO date of the last row. Informational; the last timeline key must land here."}
    timeline:
      type: array
      description: Keyframes mapping a clip frame to a date. Linear between keys, so repeat a date to hold, and use close frames to speed up. The date index is floored for display.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [atFrame, date]
        properties:
          atFrame: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          date: {type: string}
    freezeAt:
      type: object
      description: Pause the timeline at atFrame on a highlight (by sha prefix) and draw a spotlight card around it. The timeline resumes after holdFrames.
      properties:
        atFrame: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
        highlight: {type: string, description: "sha prefix of a highlight."}
        date: {type: string, description: "Optional override of the spotlight day."}
        holdFrames: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
        cardDelay: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
        label: {type: string}
    footnote: {type: string, description: Small mono text bottom-left.}
    variant:
      type: string
      enum: [paper, dark]
    layout:
      type: string
      enum: [full, panel]
      description: Transparent date and counters, contain-fit to the authored box; full keeps the complete ledger.
    width: {type: number}
    height: {type: number}
    x: {type: number}
    y: {type: number}
    binDays: {type: integer, minimum: 1, maximum: 60, description: Days per heartbeat bar. 11 gives 34 bars for the 374-day window.}
    scrollFrames: {type: integer, minimum: 2, maximum: 40, description: Frames a stamp list scroll takes.}

schema_version: 1
id: am-discord
kind: effect
pack_id: astrid_motion
short_description: Pixel-styled Discord channel reconstruction with stepped camera, highlighter and annotation.
description: A 1280-px Discord-style channel window in crisp UI, not a screenshot, with no Discord logo. Messages stack from the bottom in time order with joins and date dividers. Dividers flip split-flap through the days between dates. fit content hugs the window to the post, and camera steps integer push-ins. Highlighter, underline, strike, circle and annotation decorations step on whole frames. Joins and reactions are illustrative.
keywords:
  - discord
  - chat
  - reconstruction
  - announcement
  - reactions
  - joins
  - split-flap
  - camera
  - highlighter
  - pixel
outputs:
  - name: clip
    type: clip
    artifact_type: clip/visual
    description: Transparent Discord window overlay, centred on the frame.
metadata:
  label: AM Discord
  description: Pixel-styled Discord channel reconstruction with a content-fit window, stepped camera, highlighter, circle and annotation.
  whenToUse: Use for the announcement and the follow-up reaction beats. Pass the post as one message with its lines, verbatim, with real timestamps. Mark echo words with {u:word}. Use fit content for a hero post, camera for a stepped push-in on a word, and keep joins and reactions labelled illustrative with the badge.
  role: "card"
  text: ["messages[].lines"]
  summary: "{server} {channel} chat reconstruction"
  geometry: {"position":null,"scale":null,"full_frame":false}
  units: {"frames":["camera[].at","circle[].at","composer.startAt","messages[].appearAt"]}
defaults:
  server: OSAI
  channel: "# announcements"
  channels:
    - "# announcements"
    - "# general"
    - "# testing"
  sidebar: true
  fit: frame
  minHeight: 360
  messages: []
  dateDividers: []
  reactions: []
  joins: []
  underline: []
  strike: []
  highlight: []
  circle: []
  annotation: []
  camera: []
  badge: "RECONSTRUCTION · REACTIONS & JOINS ILLUSTRATIVE"
  frame:
    width: 1280
    height: 720
    radius: 12
    outline: "#25241F"
    shadow: 12
  jumpFrames: 12
  typeStepFrames: 2
dependencies:
  js_packages: []
  python_requirements: []
schema:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: true
  properties:
    server:
      type: string
    channel:
      type: string
      description: Channel name shown in the header, verbatim, for example "# announcements".
    channels:
      type: array
      items: {type: string}
      description: Sidebar channel names. The one equal to channel is highlighted.
    sidebar:
      type: boolean
      description: Show the channel sidebar. false hides it and widens the chat.
    fit:
      type: string
      enum: [frame, content]
      description: frame keeps the frame height. content hugs the window to the visible messages, snapping as they land, never below minHeight.
    minHeight:
      type: integer
      minimum: 180
      description: Minimum window height in px for fit content.
    messages:
      type: array
      description: Messages in posting order. Adjacent messages from the same author, tag and time render as one block. lines are paragraphs. @everyone is a mention; {u:word} marks a word.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [author, lines, appearAt]
        properties:
          author: {type: string}
          tag: {type: string, description: "Server tag shown beside the name, for example OSAI."}
          avatarColor: {type: string, description: "Hex fill for the avatar."}
          time: {type: string, description: "Timestamp shown verbatim, for example 26/10/2025 19:29."}
          lines: {type: array, items: {type: string}}
          appearAt: {type: integer, minimum: 0, description: "Clip frame the message lands on."}
          typeOn: {type: boolean, description: "Reveal characters in typeStepFrames steps."}
    dateDividers:
      type: array
      description: Date dividers. A divider after the first flips through the days between the two dates over jumpFrames, then lands.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [label, at]
        properties:
          label: {type: string, description: "A date such as 23 December 2025."}
          at: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          jump: {type: boolean, description: "Flip through the intermediate dates. Defaults to true after the first divider."}
    reactions:
      type: array
      items:
        type: object
        required: [emoji, startAt]
        properties:
          emoji: {type: string, description: "Unicode emoji, or a pixel icon URL or path."}
          countFrom: {type: integer}
          countTo: {type: integer}
          startAt: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          stepFrames: {type: integer, minimum: 1, description: "Frames per count step."}
          onMessage: {type: integer, minimum: 0, description: "Message index to attach to. Defaults to the latest message posted by startAt."}
          mine: {type: boolean, description: "Draw the blurple reacted state."}
    joins:
      type: array
      description: System join lines, in time order. Stacking accelerates when the at gaps shrink.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [name, at]
        properties:
          name: {type: string}
          at: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          time: {type: string}
    underline:
      type: array
      description: Orange underline that draws in over 6 frames under the first matching word.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [word, at]
        properties:
          word: {type: string}
          at: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          color: {type: string}
          onMessage: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    strike:
      type: array
      description: Two-step strike-through. Rust on the frame at, orange offset by one frame after.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [word, at]
        properties:
          word: {type: string}
          at: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          onMessage: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    highlight:
      type: array
      description: Vox-style marker swipe behind the word. A bar the height of cap height plus about 3 px either side, with 2 px stepped ragged ends, wipes across in 4 stepped frames.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [word, at]
        properties:
          word: {type: string}
          at: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          color: {type: string, description: "Hex, default #ED6B23."}
          alpha: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1, description: "Default 0.45."}
          onMessage: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    circle:
      type: array
      description: Rust hand-drawn ellipse around the word, drawn in 6 stepped segments.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [word, at]
        properties:
          word: {type: string}
          at: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          onMessage: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    annotation:
      type: array
      description: Small Departure Mono callout card above the word, joined by an orange connector.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [word, at, text]
        properties:
          word: {type: string}
          at: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          text: {type: string}
          onMessage: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
    camera:
      type: array
      description: Stepped integer push-ins of the whole window. Each step snaps on its frame; focus is in window px and lands on the frame centre.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [at, zoom]
        properties:
          at: {type: integer, minimum: 0}
          zoom: {type: integer, enum: [1, 2, 3]}
          focus:
            type: object
            properties:
              x: {type: number}
              y: {type: number}
    badge:
      type: string
      description: Mono label at the window's bottom-right. Empty string hides it.
    frame:
      type: object
      description: Window width, maximum height, corner radius, outline colour and hard offset shadow in px.
      properties:
        width: {type: integer}
        height: {type: integer}
        radius: {type: integer}
        outline: {type: string}
        shadow: {type: integer}
    jumpFrames:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      description: Frames a divider flip lasts.
    typeStepFrames:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
      description: Frames per typed character.

schema_version: 1
id: am-droste
kind: effect
pack_id: astrid_motion
short_description: Endless recursive zoom into a screen inside a pixel plate, on stepped moves.
description: The plate (clip.asset) holds itself inside its own screen rect (screen, logical px), again and again. The camera zooms about the recursion's fixed point, so level n arrives framed exactly as level 0 was. moves [{at, to, frames}] jump between levels on stepFrames steps with ease-out spacing; creep adds a slow stepped drift; depthTint darkens each deeper level.
keywords:
- droste
- recursion
- zoom
- screen
- loop
- pixel
outputs:
- name: clip
  type: clip
  artifact_type: clip/visual
  description: AM Droste overlay.
metadata:
  label: AM Droste
  description: Endless recursive zoom into a screen inside a pixel plate, on stepped moves.
  whenToUse: Use for recursion beats (tools to build the tool, a screen within a screen). Measure the plate's screen rect on the 320x180 grid first.
  role: "plate"
  summary: "Endless recursive zoom into a screen"
  geometry: {"position":null,"scale":null,"full_frame":true}
defaults: {}
dependencies:
  js_packages: []
  python_requirements: []
schema:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: true
  properties:
    src:
      type: string
    screen:
      type: object
      description: '{x, y, w, h} logical px of the screen inside the plate.'
    start:
      type: number
    moves:
      type: array
      description: '[{at (frame), to (level), frames}]'
    creep:
      type: number
      description: Levels per second between moves.
    stepFrames:
      type: integer
      minimum: 1
    depthTint:
      type: number
      minimum: 0
      maximum: 0.5
    maxLevel:
      type: integer
      minimum: 0
    background:
      type: string

schema_version: 1
id: am-flap
kind: effect
pack_id: astrid_motion
short_description: "Split-flap readout that flips through a drum to each target, left to right."
description: "Dark split-flap tiles with a 1 px split line and Departure Mono glyphs. values is a keyframed list of targets; each tile flips through the intermediate glyphs on two-frame steps, and tiles start one stagger apart (left to right). Positions snap to the 6 px grid. Use it for dates, counters and short words. Optional accentIndex paints characters orange, and an optional caption sits above the strip."
keywords:
  - flap
  - split-flap
  - departure-board
  - readout
  - date
  - counter
  - pixel
  - mono
outputs:
  - name: clip
    type: clip
    artifact_type: clip/visual
    description: Split-flap readout overlay.
metadata:
  label: AM Flap
  description: Split-flap readout with stepped drum flips and staggered tiles.
  whenToUse: Use for a date, number or short word that changes on screen, such as a days-since counter or a date that ticks day by day. Keep every value the same length (shorter values are padded with spaces). Flip steps are two frames by default.
  role: "card"
  text: ["values[].text"]
  summary: "Split-flap readout"
  geometry: {"position":["x","y"],"scale":null,"full_frame":false}
  units: {"frames":["values[].at"]}
dependencies:
  js_packages: []
  python_requirements: []
defaults:
  values:
    - {text: "26.10.25", at: 0}
  tileW: 60
  tileH: 84
  gap: 6
  color: "#F7F4ED"
  tileColor: "#25241F"
  accentIndex: []
  accentColor: "#ED6B23"
  x: 96
  y: 96
  align: left
  label: ""
  labelColor: "#615E55"
  stagger: 2
  stepFrames: 2
schema:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: false
  properties:
    values:
      type: array
      minItems: 1
      description: Keyframed targets. at is the frame (relative to the clip) when the flip toward text begins.
      items:
        type: object
        required: [text, at]
        properties:
          text: {type: string}
          at: {type: number}
    tileW: {type: number, minimum: 6, description: Tile width in px. Snaps to 6.}

      - 3d
      - cycles
      - eevee
      - animation

            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: engine
            flag: --engine
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: device

            optional: true

          - input: samples

          - input: frames

            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: fps

            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: denoise

            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: blender

            optional: true
            repeatable: false

            optional: true
            repeatable: false

            optional: true

            repeatable: false

            optional: true

schema_version: 1
id: always_sunny
title: Always Sunny Script Pipeline
provider:
  name: deepseek
  model: deepseek-v4-pro
  endpoint: https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions
  api_key_env: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
  timeout_seconds: 320
defaults:
  candidates: 1
  rough_attempts: 5
  select_best: false
  rough_temperature: 1.8
  synth_temperature: 1.1
  voice_temperature: 1.0
  judge_temperature: 0.2
  max_tokens: 8192
  judge_max_tokens: 1024
prompt: >-
  Write a very short It's Always Sunny in Philadelphia-style bar scene, about
  30 seconds of screen time. The gang tries to turn an ordinary minor
  inconvenience into a selfish business scheme. Keep it to 10-14 short lines,
  mostly overlapping argument. No laugh tags and no studio-audience rhythm.
prompts:
  rough_system: >-
    You are a dark farce comedy writer. You write fast, selfish, argumentative
    bar scenes where every character believes they are the only rational person
    in the room.
  synth_system: >-
    You are a structure editor for chaotic ensemble comedy. Thread multiple
    rough attempts into one escalating bar argument with a bad plan, a worse
    justification, and a quick reversal.
  synth_template: |
    Below are {rough_attempts} attempts at a short ensemble bar scene.

    Original brief:
    {prompt}

    Build one coherent short scene from the strongest material.

    Rules for this pass:
    - Center the scene on a selfish plan that should obviously fail.
    - Keep the setting grounded in a grimy neighborhood bar or a back office.
    - Make the characters interrupt, accuse, reframe, and escalate.
    - The comedy should come from bad incentives, denial, and group delusion.
    - Do not add laugh tags, applause tags, or sitcom audience beats.
    - End on a hard turn or an immediately worse idea.
    - Output only the script.

    ATTEMPTS:

    {attempts_blob}
  voice_system: |
    You are a voice pass editor for a chaotic bar ensemble comedy. Keep the structure and line count, but sharpen each line toward selfish motive, defensive denial, or a bad-faith argument.

    VOICE RULES:

    DENNIS is controlled, grandiose, and chillingly image-obsessed. He should sound like he is managing a brand crisis around himself.

    DEE is combative, insecure, and desperate to be credited. She attacks status and fairness.

    MAC is overconfident, physical, and invents rules that flatter him.

    CHARLIE is literal, grimy, and strangely practical in the wrong direction.

    FRANK is blunt, venal, and excited when the plan becomes worse.

    Do not add laugh tags, applause tags, or audience cues. Output only the corrected script.
  voice_template: |
    Here is the draft scene. Rewrite only lines that violate the voice rules. Preserve the structure, order, and approximate line count.

    DRAFT:

    {draft_scene}
  judge_system: >-
    You are judging Always Sunny-style short bar scenes. Pick the strongest
    candidate for selfish motive, ensemble argument, escalating bad logic,
    grimy specificity, and absence of laugh tags or studio-audience rhythm.
    Return strict JSON only:
    {"winner": <1-based index>, "reason": "<one concise paragraph>"}.

schema_version: 1
id: seinfeld
title: Seinfeld Script Pipeline
provider:
  name: deepseek
  model: deepseek-v4-pro
  endpoint: https://api.deepseek.com/v1/chat/completions
  api_key_env: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY
  timeout_seconds: 320
defaults:
  candidates: 1
  rough_attempts: 5
  select_best: false
  rough_temperature: 2.0
  synth_temperature: 1.0
  voice_temperature: 1.0
  judge_temperature: 0.2
  max_tokens: 8192
  judge_max_tokens: 1024
prompt: >-
  Write a VERY SHORT Seinfeld scene - about 30 seconds of screen time. Keep it
  to 8-12 short lines of dialogue total. Kramer bursts in EXTREMELY excited
  about open source AI. George is skeptical / dismissive. Jerry is confused -
  keeps interrupting with 'Who?' / 'What?' because none of the names or terms
  register. End on a button (one clean closing line). Format as a script:
  NAME: line. No stage directions beyond the opening.
prompts:
  rough_system: >-
    You are a comedy writer with deep knowledge of Seinfeld's voice and rhythm.
    You write tight, fast scenes - no fat.
  synth_system: >-
    You are a comedy writer with a deep ear for Seinfeld's rhythm. Your one job
    in this pass is STRUCTURE - turning multiple rough attempts into a single
    coherent scene. Don't worry about polishing character voices yet; that's a
    later pass. Just thread the best material.
  synth_template: |
    Below are {rough_attempts} attempts at a short scene.

    Original brief:
    {prompt}

    Pick the strongest weird ideas, specific name-jokes, and character-true beats from across the attempts, and weave them into ONE coherent ~12-line scene. Loose threading - connected enough to flow, not so neat it reads as a sketch.

    Rules for this pass:
    - Preserve the brief's requested wackiness level: funny, wacky, somewhat grounded in reality, and also over the top.
    - Choose one concrete, playable modern-life problem or object as the scene engine.
    - Keep the absurdity practical: Kramer's scheme can be ridiculous, but it should involve specific objects, errands, apartments, neighbors, dating, food, money, etiquette, or daily inconvenience.
    - Open with a one-line stage direction: location + what each character is doing.
    - Kramer bursts in early.
    - Include the "puffy shirt" callback if any attempt has it.
    - Add a small physical beat inline somewhere mid-scene.
    - End on an action or exit line, not a clever metaphor.
    - No laugh tags this pass. Just dialogue.
    - Output only the script. No commentary, no headers.

    ATTEMPTS:

    {attempts_blob}
  voice_system: |
    You are a script doctor for Seinfeld. You receive a structurally-correct draft scene and your ONLY job is to fix lines that violate character voice. You do NOT restructure, reorder, add, or remove lines. You replace individual lines that sound wrong with versions that sound right. After the voice pass, you insert laugh tags.

    CHARACTER VOICES - concrete rules:

    GEORGE doesn't construct cute analogies. He panics, catastrophizes, and complains about specific people. His comedy comes from his neuroses leaking out, not from clever metaphors.

    JERRY's voice is flat and declarative, not literary. He repeats himself slightly.

    KRAMER is concrete-absurd, not ideological or abstract. He physicalizes everything.

    LAUGH TAGS - after the voice fixes, insert at most 5 tags total, only on the biggest beats. Forms: [LAUGHTER], [BIG LAUGHTER], [LAUGHTER AND APPLAUSE]. Plus [APPLAUSE] on Kramer's entrance and [END SCENE] at the end. Do not tag every line.

    Output only the corrected script. No commentary.
  voice_template: |
    Here is the draft scene. Find lines that violate the character-voice rules and rewrite only those lines in place. Leave any line that already sounds right untouched. Do not change the structure, the order, or the count of lines. Then insert the laugh tags per the rules above.

    DRAFT:

    {draft_scene}
  judge_system: >-
    You are judging generated Seinfeld-style short scene scripts. Pick the
    single strongest candidate for concrete Kramer physical absurdity, Jerry's
    flat confusion, George's neurotic specificity, coherent escalation, and
    sparse laugh tags. Return strict JSON only:
    {"winner": <1-based index>, "reason": "<one concise paragraph>"}.

  human_review:
    name: Human Review
    version: '1.0'
    short_description: Serve a small HTML page locally, collect human decisions as JSON, block until submit.
    description: Generic human-gate primitive. Spins up a localhost HTTP server, serves a project-supplied --html page, exposes
      --data as /data.json (read-only), accepts POST /save (partial state, per keypress) and POST /submit (final, schema-validated,
      server exits 0). Reusable by any orchestrator that needs a human in the loop — dataset review, eval-grid pick, arrangement
      approval. Token-authenticated POSTs.
    keywords:
    - human
    - review
    - gate
    - browser
    - form
    - annotate
    - attested
    inputs:
    - name: html
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Direct HTML file or directory served at /. Omit when assets_bundle supplies the HTML directory.
    - name: data
      type: file
      required: true
      description: JSON file served read-only at /data.json.
    - name: serve
      type: string
      required: false
      default: __none__
      description: Repeatable static mount as <prefix>=<dir> (e.g. /clips=runs/x/accepted).
    - name: state
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Partial-state path. POST /save writes here per keystroke; GET /state.json returns contents or 404.
    - name: assets_bundle
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Bounded ZIP containing human-review-assets.json, an HTML directory root, and optional static mounts.
    - name: state_schema_bundle
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Bounded ZIP containing the unchanged M17 run-state, review-decision, and filter-stats schemas.
    - name: state_schema_entry
      type: string
      required: false
      default: run-state.schema.json
      description: Entry schema name inside state_schema_bundle.
    - name: response_schema
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Optional JSON schema validating /submit bodies (jsonschema strict mode).
    - name: port
      type: integer
      required: false
      default: 0
      description: Explicit port, or 0 for auto-pick. Default 0.
    - name: no_open
      type: boolean
      required: false
      default: false
      description: Skip auto-launching the browser. Default false.
    - name: timeout
      type: integer
      required: false
      default: 0
      description: Exit nonzero if no /submit by this many seconds. 0 = unlimited.
    outputs:
    - name: decisions
      type: file
      path_template: '{out}/human_review.final.json'
      description: Validated submit body.
    - name: state_result
      type: file
      path_template: '{out}/state_result.json'

      mode: subprocess
      network: false
    cache:

    metadata:

        - input: data

        - input: serve

          optional: true

        - input: state

          optional: true
        - input: assets_bundle

          - --out

            optional: false
          - input: prompt
            flag: --prompt
            optional: false
          - input: env_file
            flag: --env-file
            optional: true
    inputs:
      - name: clip
        type: file
        required: true
        description: Video clip to score with Foley audio (mp4/mov/webm, <=15s recommended).
      - name: prompt
        type: string
        required: true

            repeatable: true
            optional: true
          - input: video_ref
            flag: --video-ref
            repeatable: true
            optional: true
          - input: audio_ref
            flag: --audio-ref
            repeatable: true
            optional: true
          - input: duration
            flag: --duration
            optional: true
          - input: aspect_ratio
            flag: --aspect-ratio
            optional: true
          - input: env_file
            flag: --env-file
            optional: true

    inputs:

        type: file
        required: false

      - name: overlap

        required: false

      - name: trim

        required: false

      - name: env_file

        required: false

      - name: vlm_concurrency

      - name: foley_concurrency

files.astrid/packs/h3_av/pack.yaml:
schema_version: 3
id: h3_av
name: Astrid H3 audiovisual transformations
version: 0.1.0
status: experimental
domain: generation
stability: experimental
support: project
visibility: visible
permissions:
- id: project_files
  reason: Reads source media, references, masks, and writes attempt-local preparation and
    result artifacts.
- id: subprocess
  reason: Uses ffprobe/ffmpeg and the VibeComfy executor for media preparation and generation.
- id: accelerator
  reason: H3 generation requires a CUDA-capable ComfyUI runtime.
- id: network
  reason: The transform process opens no sockets itself; it coordinates runpod.* and vibecomfy
    child capabilities, which declare their own network_policy for the RunPod control plane
    (api.runpod.io and related hosts) and the managed ComfyUI session. Model and custom-node
    sources (huggingface.co, github.com) are declared for the managed worker, not fetched here.
- id: external_services
  reason: The transform may target a managed RunPod worker through the existing runtime contract.
description: Prepare, compile, execute, compose, and verify flexible MiniMax H3 audiovisual

files.astrid/packs/iteration/pack.yaml:
schema_version: 3
id: iteration
name: Astrid Iteration
version: 1.0.0
status: active
domain: development
stability: stable
support: core
permissions:
- id: subprocess
  reason: Runs iteration assembly and experiment actions as subprocesses.
- id: project_files
  reason: Reads iteration manifests and writes timeline and asset files.
description: Builds an iteration video from runtime-owned run provenance — discovers
  candidate runs through the generated client, scores quality, and assembles a canonical
  iteration timeline plus render-ready hype inputs. Also provides provider-independent
  experiment preparation and review.
keywords:
- iteration
- provenance
- runtime
- quality
- timeline
- hype
- video
- assemble
- experiment
- review
- provider-independent
capabilities:
- collect_runtime_provenance
- score_iteration_quality
- assemble_iteration_timeline
- emit_render_adapter
- experiment_prepare
- experiment_review
- experiment_import
- experiment_review_session
documentation:
  kind: skill
  path: docs/SKILL.md
agent:
  purpose: 'Use to turn runtime-owned run history into an iteration video artifact:
    discover provenance/quality from the selected project runtime, then assemble the
    canonical iteration timeline and render-compatible hype inputs.'
  do_not_use_for: Not for raw video editing or clip trimming (use the media pack)
    or final video rendering (use the rendering pack on the emitted hype adapter).
  normal_entrypoints:
  - iteration.assemble
actions:
  assemble:
    name: Iteration Assemble
    version: '1.0'
    short_description: Adapt runtime-materialized iteration data into result-only
      timeline and render artifacts.
    description: Adapt runtime-materialized iteration inputs into result-only iteration
      artifacts and render-compatible hype inputs.
    keywords:
    - iteration
    - video
    - assemble
    - render
    - hype
    - adapt
    conditions:
    - input: prepare_dir
      kind: requires_input
    inputs:
    - description: Attempt directory containing runtime-materialized iteration manifest
        and quality inputs.
      name: prepare_dir
      required: true
      type: directory
    outputs:
    - description: Canonical iteration timeline.
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: timeline
      path_template: '{out}/iteration.timeline.json'
      type: file
      artifact_type: timeline
    - description: Final iteration manifest.
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: manifest
      path_template: '{out}/iteration.manifest.json'
      type: file
    - description: Iteration HTML report.
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: report
      path_template: '{out}/iteration.report.html'
      type: file
    - description: Copied quality report with assembly status.
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: quality
      path_template: '{out}/iteration.quality.json'
      type: file
    - description: Render-compatible hype timeline adapter.
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: hype_timeline
      path_template: '{out}/hype.timeline.json'
      type: file
      artifact_type: timeline
    - description: Render-compatible hype assets adapter.
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: hype_assets
      path_template: '{out}/hype.assets.json'
      type: file
      artifact_type: timeline/assets
    cache:
      mode: none
    isolation:
      mode: subprocess
      network: false
    metadata:
      output_result_manifest: true
      runtime_entrypoint: main
      runtime_file: actions/assemble/run.py
      runtime_module: astrid.packs.iteration.actions.assemble.run
    invocation:
      kind: command
      command:
        argv:
        - '{python_exec}'
        - -m
        - astrid.packs.iteration.actions.assemble.run
        - --prepare-dir
        - '{prepare_dir}'
        - --out
        - '{out}'
    graph:
      consumes:
      - iteration_manifest
      - iteration_quality
      provides:
      - iteration_timeline
      - iteration_report
      - render_adapter
    resources:
    - kind: implementation
      path: actions/assemble/__init__.py
    - kind: implementation
      path: actions/assemble/run.py
    - kind: documentation
      path: actions/assemble/STAGE.md
  experiment_import:
    name: Experiment Import
    version: '1.0'
    short_description: Import an unmanaged run root into an experiment without rewriting
      history or guessing ambiguous associations.
    description: Import an unmanaged/legacy run root (e.g. Discord-command POC) into
      a provider-independent experiment with an honest import report. Read-only over
      source evidence; idempotent and byte-stable.
    keywords:
    - experiment
    - import
    - legacy
    - discord
    - provider-independent
    - idempotent
    - capture
    conditions:
    - input: root
      kind: requires_input
    inputs:
    - description: Unmanaged run root directory (timestamped submission subdirectories).
      name: root
      required: true
      type: directory
    - description: Optional JSON file of manual subdir -> {prompt, seed, label} mappings.
      name: mapping
      required: false
      type: file
    - description: Optional JSON file with a rubric array (defaults to a generic 0/1
        usable-output rubric).
      name: rubric_file
      required: false
      type: file
    - description: Project slug for the imported experiment (defaults to the root
        dir name).
      name: project_slug
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: Experiment id (defaults to <project-slug>-import). Must match ^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*$.
      name: experiment_id
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: Experiment title (defaults to 'Imported runs from <root name>').
      name: title
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: Experiment question (defaults to 'What do these legacy runs show?').
      name: question
      required: false
      type: string
    outputs:
    - description: Imported experiment definition referencing synthesized run ids.
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: experiment
      path_template: '{out}/experiment.json'
      type: file
    - description: 'Honest import report: counts, ambiguous/screenshot-only cases,
        dedup, capture gaps.'
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: import_report
      path_template: '{out}/import.report.json'
      type: file
    - description: 'Synthesized imported run tree: one subdir per case with manifest.json
        and hardlinked source media.'
      mode: create_or_replace
      name: runs
      path_template: '{out}/runs'
      type: directory
    cache:
      mode: none
    isolation:
      mode: subprocess
      network: false
      env_passthrough:
      - ASTRID_REPO_ROOT
    metadata:
      output_result_manifest: true
      requires_timeline: false
      runtime_entrypoint: main
      runtime_file: actions/experiment_import/run.py
      runtime_module: astrid.packs.iteration.actions.experiment_import.run
    invocation:
      kind: command
      command:
        argv:
        - '{python_exec}'
        - -m
        - astrid.packs.iteration.actions.experiment_import.run
        - --root
        - '{root}'
        - --out
        - '{out}'
        input_args:
        - input: mapping
          flag: --mapping
          optional: true
        - input: rubric_file
          flag: --rubric-file
          optional: true
        - input: project_slug
          flag: --project-slug
          optional: true
        - input: experiment_id
          flag: --experiment-id
          optional: true
        - input: title
          flag: --title
          optional: true
        - input: question
          flag: --question
          optional: true
    graph:
      consumes:
      - unmanaged_run_root
      - optional_manual_mappings
      provides:
      - imported_experiment_definition
      - import_report
    resources:
    - kind: implementation
      path: actions/experiment_import/__init__.py
    - kind: implementation
      path: actions/experiment_import/run.py
    - kind: documentation
      path: actions/experiment_import/STAGE.md
  experiment_prepare:

schema_version: 1
id: animated-media-transform
kind: effect
pack_id: local
dependencies:
  js_packages: []
  python_requirements: []
short_description: Animate one managed image or video through editable position, size and opacity keyframes.
description: Clip-local transform keyframes interpolate in authored canvas pixels. Optional source playback segments independently preserve trims, speed changes and deliberate source resets inside one timeline clip. Uses the same component in live preview and Remotion rendering.
keywords: [media, video, image, zoom, pan, fade, keyframes]
metadata:
  label: Animated Media Transform
  whenToUse: Use one held effect clip with a managed asset to animate a video or image without slicing it into per-frame timeline clips. Edit params.keyframes and params.sourceSegments in the canonical timeline document.
  clipTypeAliases: [animated-media-transform]
defaults:
  fit: contain
  keyframes:
    - {at: 0, x: 0, y: 0, width: 1920, height: 1080, opacity: 1}
schema:
  type: object
  additionalProperties: false
  required: [keyframes]
  properties:
    fit: {type: string, enum: [contain, cover, fill]}
    keyframes:
      type: array
      minItems: 1
      description: Increasing clip-local seconds with x/y/width/height in canvas pixels. Values interpolate linearly and clamp outside the range.
      items:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [at, x, y, width, height, opacity]
        properties:
          at: {type: number, minimum: 0}
          x: {type: number}
          y: {type: number}
          width: {type: number, exclusiveMinimum: 0}
          height: {type: number, exclusiveMinimum: 0}
          opacity: {type: number, minimum: 0, maximum: 1}
    sourceSegments:
      type: array
      minItems: 1
      description: Video playback sections starting at clip-local seconds; first at 0. Rounded frame boundaries must be distinct.
      items:
        type: object
        additionalProperties: false
        required: [at, sourceStart, speed]
        properties:
          at: {type: number, minimum: 0}
          sourceStart: {type: number, minimum: 0}
          speed: {type: number, exclusiveMinimum: 0}

schema_version: 3
id: media
name: Media
version: 0.1.0
status: active
domain: media
stability: stable
support: core
permissions:
  - id: subprocess
    reason: Runs ffmpeg for video clip extraction and audio remuxing/normalization.
  - id: project_files
    reason: Reads source video files and writes output clips.
  - id: network
    reason: Optional speech repair executor calls fal.ai LavaSR; GIF search calls remote media APIs.
  - id: environment
    reason: Reads FAL_KEY for fal.ai speech repair and GIPHY_API_KEY for GIF search.
description: Media processing tools, including clip extraction, weak-mic speech repair, and remote GIF search.
keywords:
  - video
  - clip
  - ffmpeg
  - extract
  - trim
  - segment
  - lossless
  - audio
  - speech
  - lavasr
  - gif
  - sticker
  - giphy
capabilities:
  - extract_clip
  - trim_video
  - repair_speech
  - search_gifs
  - download_remote_media
documentation:
  kind: skill
  path: docs/SKILL.md
agent:
  purpose: "Use when you need to trim media segments, repair weak-mic speech in a video clip, or search/download GIF and sticker assets."
  do_not_use_for: "Not for building iteration videos from run history (use the iteration pack) or final timeline rendering (use the rendering pack)."
  normal_entrypoints:
    - media.clip_extract
    - media.speech_repair_lavasr
    - media.gif_search
actions:
  clip_extract:
    name: Clip Extract
    version: "1.0"
    short_description: Extract a clip segment from a video using ffmpeg stream copy.
    description: Extract a clip segment from a source video using ffmpeg -ss (start time) and -t (duration) with stream copy (-c copy) for lossless, fast extraction.
    keywords:
      - video
      - clip
      - ffmpeg
      - extract
      - trim
      - segment
    invocation:
      kind: command
      command:
        argv:
          - "{python_exec}"
          - "-m"
          - "astrid.packs.media.actions.clip_extract.run"
          - "--input"
          - "{input}"
          - "--start"
          - "{start}"
          - "--dur"
          - "{dur}"
          - "--output"
          - "{output}"
    inputs:
      - name: input
        type: file
        required: true
        description: Runtime-managed source video object reference; materialized as a file for the action.
      - name: start
        type: number
        required: true
        description: Start time in seconds.
      - name: dur
        type: number
        required: true
        description: Duration in seconds.
    outputs:
      - name: output
        type: file
        path_template: "{out}/clip.mp4"
        description: The clipped video file.
    resources:
      - kind: implementation
        path: actions/clip_extract/run.py
      - kind: documentation
        path: actions/clip_extract/STAGE.md
    cache:
      mode: none
    isolation:
      mode: subprocess
      network: false
      binaries:
        - ffmpeg
    metadata:
      runtime_entrypoint: main
      runtime_file: actions/clip_extract/run.py
      runtime_module: astrid.packs.media.actions.clip_extract.run
      output_result_manifest: true
  gif_search:
    name: GIF Search
    version: "1.0"
    short_description: Search GIPHY for GIF or sticker assets and optionally download a selected rendition.
    description: Search GIPHY for GIFs or stickers, normalize the result metadata, write results.json and preview.html, and optionally download one selected rendition as MP4 or GIF for timeline use.
    keywords:
      - gif
      - gifs
      - sticker
      - stickers
      - giphy
      - search
      - download
      - asset
      - media
    invocation:
      kind: command
      command:
        argv:
          - "{python_exec}"
          - "-m"
          - "astrid.packs.media.actions.gif_search.run"
          - "--query"
          - "{query}"
          - "--out"
          - "{out}"
        input_args:
          - input: provider
            flag: --provider
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: media_kind
            flag: --media-kind
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: limit
            flag: --limit
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: rating
            flag: --rating
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: env_file
            flag: --env-file
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: download_index
            flag: --download-index
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: download_id
            flag: --download-id
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
    inputs:
      - name: query
        type: string
        required: true
        description: Search query to send to the GIF provider.
      - name: provider
        type: string
        required: false
        description: Provider to use. Currently only 'giphy' is implemented.
      - name: media_kind
        type: string
        required: false
        description: "Asset kind to search: 'gif' or 'sticker'."
      - name: limit
        type: integer
        required: false
        description: Maximum number of results to return.
      - name: rating
        type: string
        required: false
        description: GIPHY rating filter, such as g, pg, pg-13, or r.
      - name: env_file
        type: file
        required: false
        description: Optional Runtime-managed .env object containing GIPHY_API_KEY.
      - name: download_index
        type: integer
        required: false
        description: Optional zero-based result index to download.
      - name: download_id
        type: string
        required: false
        description: Optional provider result id to download.
    outputs:
      - name: results
        type: file
        path_template: "{out}/results.json"
        description: Normalized search result metadata.
      - name: preview
        type: file
        path_template: "{out}/preview.html"
        description: Static preview page for browsing returned assets.
    resources:
      - kind: implementation
        path: actions/gif_search/run.py
      - kind: documentation
        path: actions/gif_search/STAGE.md
    scoped_configs:
      - credentials.giphy
    cache:
      mode: none
    isolation:
      mode: subprocess
      network: true
      secrets_required:
        - GIPHY_API_KEY
    metadata:
      runtime_entrypoint: main
      runtime_file: actions/gif_search/run.py
      runtime_module: astrid.packs.media.actions.gif_search.run
      output_result_manifest: true
      network_policy:
        allowed_protocols:
          - dns
          - tcp
        allowed_destinations:
          - api.giphy.com:443
        allow_redirects: false
        broker:
          host_managed: true
          kind: broker
          enforced: true
          observable: true
          route: declared-http-routes
          wrapper: astrid-generic-host
        descendant_enforcement:
          kind: broker
          validated: true
          observable: true
          route: declared-http-routes
          wrapper: astrid-generic-host
  speech_repair_lavasr:
    name: Speech Repair LavaSR
    version: "1.0"
    short_description: Repair weak-mic speech with hotter pre-lift, fal.ai LavaSR, optional DeepFilterNet3, and a final loudness pass.
    description: Extract a video section, aggressively pre-lift weak speech, run fal-ai/lava-sr, optionally run fal-ai/deepfilternet3, then remux and loudness-master the repaired audio onto the extracted video.
    keywords:
      - audio
      - speech
      - repair
      - lavasr
      - fal
      - ffmpeg
      - weak-mic
    invocation:
      kind: command
      command:
        argv:
          - "{python_exec}"
          - "-m"
          - "astrid.packs.media.actions.speech_repair_lavasr.run"
          - "--input"
          - "{input}"
          - "--start"
          - "{start}"
          - "--dur"
          - "{dur}"
          - "--output"
          - "{output}"
        input_args:
          - input: env_file
            flag: --env-file
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
          - input: deepfilternet3
            flag: --deepfilternet3
            optional: true
            repeatable: false
    inputs:
      - name: input
        type: file
        required: true
        description: Runtime-managed source video object reference; materialized as a file for the action.
        artifact_type: audio
      - name: start
        type: number
        required: true
        description: Start time in seconds within the source video.
      - name: dur
        type: number
        required: true
        description: Duration in seconds to extract and repair.
      - name: env_file
        type: file
        required: false
        description: Optional Runtime-managed .env object containing FAL_KEY.
      - name: deepfilternet3
        type: boolean
        required: false
        description: Run fal-ai/deepfilternet3 after LavaSR before final loudness mastering.
    outputs:
      - name: output
        type: file
        path_template: "{out}/speech-repair-lavasr.mp4"
        description: The extracted clip with LavaSR-repaired, loudness-mastered audio.
        artifact_type: audio
    resources:
      - kind: implementation
        path: actions/speech_repair_lavasr/__init__.py
      - kind: implementation
        path: actions/speech_repair_lavasr/run.py
      - kind: documentation
        path: actions/speech_repair_lavasr/STAGE.md
    scoped_configs:
      - credentials.fal
    cache:
      mode: none
    isolation:
      mode: subprocess
      network: true
      binaries:
        - ffmpeg
        - ffprobe
      secrets_required:
        - FAL_KEY
    metadata:
      runtime_entrypoint: main
      runtime_file: actions/speech_repair_lavasr/run.py
      runtime_module: astrid.packs.media.actions.speech_repair_lavasr.run
      output_result_manifest: true
      network_policy:
        allowed_protocols:
          - dns
          - tcp
        allowed_destinations:
          - queue.fal.run:443
          - fal.run:443
          - storage.fal.run:443
        allow_redirects: false
        broker:
          host_managed: true
          kind: broker
          enforced: true
          observable: true
          route: declared-http-routes
          wrapper: astrid-generic-host
        descendant_enforcement:
          kind: broker
          validated: true
          observable: true
          route: declared-http-routes
          wrapper: astrid-generic-host
