          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 3,
          "description": "Maximum native-cell gap for detached details to join a piece."
        },
        {
          "name": "padding",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 2,
          "description": "Transparent native cells around each trimmed sprite."
        },
        {
          "name": "scale",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 8,
          "description": "Preview magnification and on-screen size reported for one timeline scale."
        }
      ],
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "sprites",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/images",
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "Ordered native RGBA sprites, one managed output row per piece."
        },
        {
          "name": "preview",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/preview.png",
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "Indexed contact sheet at scale with nearest-neighbour pixels."
        },
        {
          "name": "report",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/report.json",
          "description": "Lattice, source boxes, sizes, and outline-integrity measurements."
        }
      ],
      "cache": {
        "mode": "none"
      },
      "isolation": {
        "mode": "subprocess",
        "network": false
      },
      "metadata": {
        "runtime_entrypoint": "main",
        "runtime_file": "actions/sprites/run.py",
        "runtime_module": "astrid.packs.pixel.actions.sprites.run",
        "output_result_manifest": true
      },
      "resources": [
        {
          "kind": "implementation",
          "path": "actions/sprites/run.py"
        },
        {
          "kind": "implementation",
          "path": "actions/_common.py"
        },
        {
          "kind": "documentation",
          "path": "actions/sprites/STAGE.md"
        }
      ]
    },
    "cutout": {
      "name": "Pixel Cutout",
      "version": "1.1.0",
      "short_description": "Remove a flat, chroma-key, or light background into hard-alpha RGBA, optionally on the snapped pixel grid.",
      "description": "Crops (optional), optionally snaps to a logical grid first (grid=auto or WxH), then removes the background: chroma (key colour, default magenta), flat (dominant border colour), or luma (light backdrop). Background connected to the border is removed; holes=true also removes enclosed key colour. The dark outline survives. Alpha is strictly 0 or 255. Optionally trims to the alpha bounding box with padding and drops small detached specks. Outputs an RGBA PNG and a JSON report.",
      "keywords": [
        "pixel",
        "pixel-art",
        "cutout",
        "transparency",
        "chroma-key",
        "background-removal",
        "alpha",
        "sprite"
      ],
      "invocation": {
        "kind": "command",
        "command": {
          "argv": [
            "{python_exec}",
            "-m",
            "astrid.packs.pixel.actions.cutout.run",
            "--image",
            "{image}",
            "--out",
            "{out}",
            "--mode",
            "{mode}",
            "--key",
            "{key}",
            "--tolerance",
            "{tolerance}",
            "--fit",
            "{fit}",
            "--trim",
            "{trim}",
            "--trim-padding",
            "{trim_padding}",
            "--keep-largest",
            "{keep_largest}",
            "--holes",
            "{holes}",
            "--allow-lossy",
            "{allow_lossy}"
          ],
          "input_args": [
            {
              "input": "crop",
              "flag": "--crop",
              "optional": true
            },
            {
              "input": "grid",
              "flag": "--grid",
              "optional": true
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "inputs": [
        {
          "name": "image",
          "type": "file",
          "required": true,
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "Managed image descriptor {digest, filename, media_type, size_bytes} from python -m astrid media import."
        },
        {
          "name": "crop",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "description": "Optional JSON-encoded {x, y, width, height} in source pixels, applied before anything else."
        },
        {
          "name": "mode",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "default": "chroma",
          "description": "chroma (key colour), flat (auto-detected border colour), or luma (light backdrop)."
        },
        {
          "name": "key",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "default": "#FF00FF",
          "description": "Key colour for chroma mode."
        },
        {
          "name": "tolerance",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 48,
          "description": "RGB distance (0-255) from the key or border colour that counts as background."
        },
        {
          "name": "grid",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "description": "auto to detect the pixel lattice, or WIDTHxHEIGHT to snap first; omit to cut at full resolution."
        },
        {
          "name": "fit",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "default": "contain",
          "description": "Fit used with an explicit grid (cover, contain or none). contain keeps the whole subject."
        },
        {
          "name": "trim",
          "type": "boolean",
          "required": false,
          "default": true,
          "description": "Crop to the alpha bounding box."
        },
        {
          "name": "trim_padding",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 2,
          "description": "Padding in output pixels around the trimmed bounding box."
        },
        {
          "name": "keep_largest",
          "type": "boolean",
          "required": false,
          "default": true,
          "description": "Drop detached specks smaller than 5% of the largest foreground component."
        },
        {
          "name": "holes",
          "type": "boolean",
          "required": false,
          "default": false,
          "description": "Also remove key-coloured pixels enclosed by the sprite (gaps between legs, chain links). For chroma keys that never occur in the art."
        },
        {
          "name": "allow_lossy",
          "type": "boolean",
          "required": false,
          "default": false,
          "description": "Override the guard against a coarse explicit grid when grid is WIDTHxHEIGHT."
        }
      ],
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "cutout",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/cutout.png",
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "RGBA PNG with hard alpha."
        },
        {
          "name": "report",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/report.json",
          "description": "Background key, bounding box, grid used, and speck statistics."
        }
      ],
      "cache": {
        "mode": "none"
      },
      "isolation": {
        "mode": "subprocess",
        "network": false
      },
      "metadata": {
        "runtime_entrypoint": "main",
        "runtime_file": "actions/cutout/run.py",
        "runtime_module": "astrid.packs.pixel.actions.cutout.run",
        "output_result_manifest": true
      },
      "resources": [
        {
          "kind": "implementation",
          "path": "actions/cutout/run.py"
        },
        {
          "kind": "implementation",
          "path": "actions/_common.py"
        },
        {
          "kind": "documentation",
          "path": "actions/cutout/STAGE.md"
        }
      ]
    },
    "snap": {
      "name": "Pixel Snap",
      "version": "1.1.0",
      "short_description": "Snap a generated image onto a logical pixel grid with mode downsampling, optional palette, and a scaled preview.",
      "description": "Crops (optional), then downsamples a managed image onto a logical pixel grid by taking each cell's modal colour, so 1 px outlines survive. The grid is either explicit (grid_width x grid_height, with fit cover/contain/none) or detected from the image's own pixel lattice (auto_grid). Optional palette (hex list or the astrid preset) or max_colors quantisation, then a nearest-neighbour preview. Outputs a grid-size native PNG, a scaled preview PNG, and a JSON report.",
      "keywords": [
        "pixel",
        "pixel-art",
        "grid",
        "palette",
        "quantize",
        "snap",
        "sprite",
        "downsample"
      ],
      "invocation": {
        "kind": "command",
        "command": {
          "argv": [
            "{python_exec}",
            "-m",
            "astrid.packs.pixel.actions.snap.run",
            "--image",
            "{image}",
            "--out",
            "{out}",
            "--auto-grid",
            "{auto_grid}",
            "--grid-width",
            "{grid_width}",
            "--grid-height",
            "{grid_height}",
            "--fit",
            "{fit}",
            "--scale",
            "{scale}",
            "--dither",
            "{dither}",
            "--allow-lossy",
            "{allow_lossy}"
          ],
          "input_args": [
            {
              "input": "crop",
              "flag": "--crop",
              "optional": true
            },
            {
              "input": "palette",
              "flag": "--palette",
              "optional": true,
              "repeatable": true
            },
            {
              "input": "max_colors",
              "flag": "--max-colors",
              "optional": true
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "inputs": [
        {
          "name": "image",
          "type": "file",
          "required": true,
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "Managed image descriptor {digest, filename, media_type, size_bytes} from python -m astrid media import."
        },
        {
          "name": "crop",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "description": "Optional JSON-encoded {x, y, width, height} in source pixels, applied before anything else."
        },
        {
          "name": "auto_grid",
          "type": "boolean",
          "required": false,
          "default": false,
          "description": "Detect the pixel-block lattice from edge periodicity instead of using grid_width/grid_height."
        },
        {
          "name": "grid_width",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 320,
          "description": "Logical grid width in cells (explicit grid only)."
        },
        {
          "name": "grid_height",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 180,
          "description": "Logical grid height in cells (explicit grid only)."
        },
        {
          "name": "fit",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "default": "cover",
          "description": "cover crops to the grid aspect, contain pads to it, none stretches the source."
        },
        {
          "name": "palette",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "description": "Preset name (astrid), comma-separated hex colours, or a list of hex colours to map cells onto."
        },
        {
          "name": "max_colors",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "description": "Quantise to this many colours (2-256) when no palette is given."
        },
        {
          "name": "scale",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 6,
          "description": "Integer nearest-neighbour factor for the preview output."
        },
        {
          "name": "dither",
          "type": "boolean",
          "required": false,
          "default": false,
          "description": "Floyd-Steinberg dithering when a palette or max_colors is applied."
        },
        {
          "name": "allow_lossy",
          "type": "boolean",
          "required": false,
          "default": false,
          "description": "Override refusal when the explicit grid is over 20 percent coarser than the drawn lattice."
        }
      ],
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "native",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/native.png",
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "Grid-size RGBA PNG with hard alpha (the true pixel art)."
        },
        {
          "name": "preview",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/preview.png",
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "Native grid scaled by an integer factor with nearest-neighbour sampling."
        },
        {
          "name": "report",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/report.json",
          "description": "Detected grid, colours used, and palette distance statistics."
        }
      ],
      "cache": {
        "mode": "none"
      },
      "isolation": {
        "mode": "subprocess",
        "network": false
      },
      "metadata": {
        "runtime_entrypoint": "main",
        "runtime_file": "actions/snap/run.py",
        "runtime_module": "astrid.packs.pixel.actions.snap.run",
        "output_result_manifest": true
      },
      "resources": [
        {
          "kind": "implementation",
          "path": "actions/snap/run.py"
        },
        {
          "kind": "implementation",
          "path": "actions/_common.py"
        },
        {
          "kind": "documentation",
          "path": "actions/snap/STAGE.md"
        }
      ]
    },
    "strip": {
      "name": "Pixel Sprite Strip",
      "version": "1.1.0",
      "short_description": "Join ordered pixel-art frames into one shared-grid horizontal sprite strip.",
      "description": "Aligns trimmed frames onto a common transparent cell, snaps every frame to the same logical grid and palette, then joins them left to right. Metadata includes the frame block consumed by am-sprite.",
      "keywords": [
        "pixel",
        "sprite",
        "strip",
        "animation",
        "am-sprite"
      ],
      "invocation": {
        "kind": "command",
        "command": {
          "argv": [
            "{python_exec}",
            "-m",
            "astrid.packs.pixel.actions.strip.run",
            "--out",
            "{out}",
            "--grid-width",
            "{grid_width}",
            "--grid-height",
            "{grid_height}",
            "--fit",
            "{fit}",
            "--fps",
            "{fps}",
            "--align",
            "{align}",
            "--allow-lossy",
            "{allow_lossy}"
          ],
          "input_args": [
            {
              "input": "frame",
              "flag": "--frame",
              "optional": false,
              "repeatable": true
            },
            {
              "input": "palette",
              "flag": "--palette",
              "optional": true,
              "repeatable": true
            },
            {
              "input": "max_colors",
              "flag": "--max-colors",
              "optional": true
            }
          ]
        }
      },
      "inputs": [
        {
          "name": "frame",
          "type": "file",
          "required": true,
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "Ordered image handles, at least two; playback follows list order."
        },
        {
          "name": "grid_width",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Shared grid width. 0 uses aligned frame width; set with grid_height."
        },
        {
          "name": "grid_height",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Shared grid height. 0 uses aligned frame height; set with grid_width."
        },
        {
          "name": "fit",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "default": "cover",
          "description": "How each frame fits an explicit grid: cover, contain or none."
        },
        {
          "name": "palette",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "description": "One palette for every frame: astrid, comma-separated hex colours, or repeated hex values."
        },
        {
          "name": "max_colors",
          "type": "integer",
          "required": false,
          "default": 0,
          "description": "Quantise all frames to 2\u2013256 colours when no palette is given; 0 disables it."
        },
        {
          "name": "fps",
          "type": "number",
          "required": false,
          "default": 8,
          "description": "Playback rate stored for am-sprite."
        },
        {
          "name": "align",
          "type": "string",
          "required": false,
          "default": "bottom",
          "description": "Pad trimmed frames to a common cell, centered horizontally and anchored bottom, center or top."
        },
        {
          "name": "allow_lossy",
          "type": "boolean",
          "required": false,
          "default": false,
          "description": "Override the guard against an explicit grid over 20 percent coarser than the drawn lattice."
        }
      ],
      "outputs": [
        {
          "name": "strip",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/strip.png",
          "artifact_type": "image",
          "description": "Horizontal RGBA sprite strip, frames left to right."
        },
        {
          "name": "metadata",
          "type": "file",
          "path_template": "{out}/strip.json",
          "description": "Frame dimensions, count, fps and am_sprite_frames metadata."
        }
      ],
      "cache": {
        "mode": "none"
      },
      "isolation": {
        "mode": "subprocess",
        "network": false
      },
      "metadata": {
        "runtime_entrypoint": "main",
        "runtime_file": "actions/strip/run.py",
        "runtime_module": "astrid.packs.pixel.actions.strip.run",
        "output_result_manifest": true
      },
      "resources": [
        {
          "kind": "implementation",
          "path": "actions/strip/run.py"
        },
        {
          "kind": "implementation",
          "path": "actions/_common.py"
        },
        {
          "kind": "documentation",
          "path": "docs/SKILL.md"
        }
      ]
    }
  }
}
files.astrid/packs/rendering/pack.yaml:
schema_version: 3
id: rendering
name: Astrid Rendering
version: 1.0.0
status: active
domain: media
stability: stable
support: core
visibility: visible
permissions:
- id: subprocess
  reason: Runs Remotion render process and ffmpeg sprite processing.
- id: project_files
  reason: Reads timeline, asset, and theme files; writes rendered video.
- id: network
  reason: Sprite sheet executor calls OpenAI GPT Image API.
description: Author, inspect, preview, and render runtime-owned timelines; visualize
  them as deterministic evidence packs; generate GPT-Image sprite sheets; and supply
  render-time animation/transition/effect elements.
keywords:
- render
- remotion
- video
- mp4
- timeline
- visualize
- evidence
- sprite-sheet
- gpt-image
- animation
capabilities:
- render_timeline
- generate_sprite_sheet
- scaffold_html_canvas_effect
agent:
  purpose: Choose this pack for runtime-owned timeline authoring and inspection, candidate
    preview/publication, finished video rendering, deterministic visual evidence,
    GPT Image sprite sheets, or canvas/WebGL post-processing effects.
  do_not_use_for: Publishing rendered output to external services.
  normal_entrypoints:
  - rendering.render
  - rendering.sprite_sheet
documentation:
  kind: skill
  path: docs/SKILL.md
actions:
  assemble_timeline:
    name: Assemble Canonical Timeline
    version: '1.0'
    short_description: Author a canonical two-child timeline from runtime-resolved
      visual outputs.
    description: Validate a fenced two-child runtime continuation and emit a deterministic
      canonical timeline authoring proposal. Timeline mutation and rendering remain
      runtime-owned.
    keywords:
    - timeline
    - assemble
    - continuation
    - runtime
    - canonical
    - video
    inputs:
    - name: resolved_children
      type: json
      required: true
      artifact_type: runtime/resolved-children
      description: Runtime-resolved continuation graph, terminal child outputs, and
        ordered CAS aggregation.
    outputs:
    - name: timeline
      type: file
      mode: create_or_replace
      path_template: '{out}/timeline.json'
      artifact_type: timeline
      description: Deterministic canonical TimelineConfig proposal.
    - name: assets
      type: file
      mode: create_or_replace
      path_template: '{out}/assets.json'
      artifact_type: timeline/assets
      description: Runtime-managed media registry proposal for the timeline clips.
    - name: authoring_proposal
      type: file
      mode: create_or_replace
      path_template: '{out}/authoring-proposal.json'
      artifact_type: timeline/authoring-proposal
      description: Typed runtime publication handoff containing the timeline and registry.
    graph:
      consumes:
      - runtime/resolved-children
      provides:
      - timeline
      - timeline/assets
      - timeline/authoring-proposal
    cache:
      mode: none
    isolation:
      mode: subprocess
      network: false
    metadata:
      runtime_entrypoint: main
      runtime_file: actions/assemble_timeline/run.py
      runtime_module: astrid.packs.rendering.actions.assemble_timeline.run
      output_result_manifest: true
      requires_timeline: false
      mutation_authority: workspace_runtime
      continuation_shape: two-child-ordered-cas-v1
    invocation:
      kind: command
      command:
        argv:
        - '{python_exec}'
        - -m
        - astrid.packs.rendering.actions.assemble_timeline.run
        - --resolved-children
        - '{resolved_children}'
        - --out
        - '{out}'
    resources:
    - kind: implementation
      path: actions/assemble_timeline/run.py
  timeline_visualize:
    name: Timeline Visualize
    version: '1.0'
    short_description: Private backend for composed timeline visualization.
    description: Internal managed executor used by the canonical timelines.visualize
      operation to inspect an exact admitted render or produce a structural revision
      diff from two host-compiled immutable bundles. This backend is not a public
      capability and must not be invoked directly.
    keywords:
    - timeline
    - visualize
    - evidence
    - agent
    - png
    inputs:
    - name: project_slug
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Owning Astrid project slug. In a project-scoped SDK invocation
        this is derived from project=<slug>; pass it for a standalone runner invocation.
    - name: timeline_slug
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Managed timeline reference by slug, UUID, or ULID; omission selects
        the project default.
    - name: shot
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Authored pinnedShotGroups[].shotId to focus.
    - name: range
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Closed-open START..END window; times are seconds or [HH:]MM:SS[.fff].
    - name: at
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Timestamp to inspect, in seconds or [HH:]MM:SS[.fff].
    - name: frame
      type: integer
      required: false
      description: Exact rendered frame number to capture; mutually exclusive with
        range and at.
    - name: clip
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Authored clip id to focus.
    - name: asset
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Canonical asset key to inspect with every timeline use.
    - name: show
      type: string
      required: false
      description: 'Add synchronized components (repeatable/comma-separated): output,
        text, audio, or inputs.'
    - name: hide
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Hide synchronized components (repeatable/comma-separated).
    - name: track
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Restrict input lanes to one or more track ids.
    - name: detail
      type: boolean
      required: false
      default: false
      description: Request detail treatment for the shared current selection.
    - name: context
      type: number
      required: false
      default: 3.0
      description: Symmetric context seconds for clip or timestamp focus.
    - name: neighbors
      type: integer
      required: false
      default: 0
      description: Previous and next clips retained on a focused clip's track.
    - name: formats
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Optional presentation format list. Choices are png or md (default
        png,md). Core machine artifacts are always written.
    - name: rendered_video
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Host-injected attempt-local rendered video; callers select it with
        render_run.
    - name: materialized_root
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Host-owned attempt-local managed object root.
    - name: materialized_objects
      type: json
      required: false
      description: Host-owned object-id to attempt-local path handoff.
    - name: timeline
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Host-injected materialized canonical timeline config for composed
        frame capture.
    - name: assets_registry
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Host-injected materialized asset registry for composed frame capture.
    - name: transcript.json
      type: file
      required: false
      description: Host-staged bytes for the hash-bound config.app.transcript declaration;
        callers cannot provide this path.
    - name: view
      type: string
      required: false
      description: 'Presentation: filmstrip (default), contact overview, bounded motion sheet, or immutable revision diff.'
      default: filmstrip
    - name: before_revision_id
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Required with view=diff; exact immutable before revision selector with no current-head fallback.
    - name: after_revision_id
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Required with view=diff; exact immutable after revision selector with no current-head fallback.
    - name: edited
      type: string
      required: false
      description: 'Diff view only: the cut numbers you meant to edit (comma-separated); a change anywhere else is a SCOPE warning.'
    - name: revision_diff
      type: json
      required: false
      description: Host-injected compiled astrid.timeline_revision_diff.v1 JSON; caller-supplied values are rejected by native preflight.
    - name: cut
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Motion cut number, picture clip id, or @seconds selector.
    - name: layers
      type: string
      required: false
      description: Repeatable/comma-separated registered visualization layer names.
    - name: beats
      type: json
      required: false
      description: Caller-resolved beats object containing beats, downbeats, and hits.
    - name: frame_budget
      type: integer

schema_version: 3
id: runpod
name: Astrid RunPod
version: 1.0.0
status: active
domain: infrastructure
stability: stable
support: core
visibility: visible
permissions:
- id: subprocess
  reason: Runs RunPod CLI commands as subprocesses.
- id: network
  reason: Calls RunPod GraphQL API for pod provisioning and management.
- id: environment
  reason: Reads RUNPOD_API_KEY for authentication.
- id: external_services
  reason: Manages cloud GPU infrastructure on RunPod.
description: Provision RunPod GPU pods, ship and run scripts on them, pull artifacts,
  and tear pods down — including a guaranteed-cleanup composite session.
keywords:
- runpod
- gpu
- provision
- exec
- pull
- teardown
- session
- ssh
capabilities:
- provision_pod
- exec_on_pod
- pull_artifacts
- teardown_pod
- run_pod_session
agent:
  purpose: Choose this pack when you need ephemeral cloud GPU compute on RunPod —
    to spin up a pod, run a script remotely, retrieve artifacts/checkpoints, and shut
    it down. Prefer runpod.session for one-shot jobs that should always clean up.
  do_not_use_for: Not for orchestrating LoRA training workflows end to end; use the
    training pack, which drives RunPod under the hood.
  normal_entrypoints:
  - runpod.session
  - runpod.provision
documentation:
  kind: skill
  path: docs/SKILL.md
actions:
  provision:
    name: RunPod Provision
    version: 0.1.0
    short_description: Provision a RunPod GPU pod and emit a pod handle for later
      exec/teardown.
    description: Provision a RunPod GPU pod and emit a pod_handle.json artifact. Does
      not terminate.
    keywords:
    - runpod
    - gpu
    - provision
    - pod
    - launch
    invocation:
      kind: command
      command:
        argv:
        - '{python_exec}'
        - -m
        - astrid.packs.runpod.actions.provision.run
        - provision
        - --produces-dir
        - '{out}/produces'
        input_args:
        - input: compute_profile
          flag: --compute-profile
          optional: true
        - input: gpu_type
          flag: --gpu-type
          optional: true
        - input: allowed_cuda_versions
          flag: --allowed-cuda-versions
          optional: true
        - input: storage_name
          flag: --storage-name
          optional: true
        - input: max_runtime_seconds
          flag: --max-runtime-seconds
          optional: true
        - input: name_prefix
          flag: --name-prefix
          optional: true
        - input: image
          flag: --image
          optional: true
        - input: container_disk_gb
          flag: --container-disk-gb
          optional: true
        - input: volume_in_gb
          flag: --volume-in-gb
          optional: true
        - input: volume_mount_path
          flag: --volume-mount-path
          optional: true
        - input: datacenter_id
          flag: --datacenter-id
          optional: true
        - input: ports
          flag: --ports
          optional: true
    inputs:
    - description: Named user compute profile. This explicit selector takes precedence
        over ASTRID_COMPUTE_PROFILE.
      name: compute_profile
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: GPU type to request (e.g. RTX 4090, A100).
      name: gpu_type
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: Comma-separated CUDA host versions for RunPod placement (e.g. 12.4,12.6).
      name: allowed_cuda_versions
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: Name of a pre-existing RunPod network storage volume.
      name: storage_name
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: Maximum runtime in seconds before the pod guard triggers.
      name: max_runtime_seconds
      required: false
      type: integer
    - description: Name prefix for the pod (used for grouping and sweeper correlation).
      name: name_prefix
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: Docker image to run on the pod.
      name: image
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: Container disk size in GB.
      name: container_disk_gb
      required: false
      type: integer
    - description: Local or network volume size in GB.
      name: volume_in_gb
      required: false
      type: integer
    - description: Mount path for the local or network volume.
      name: volume_mount_path
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: RunPod datacenter ID.
      name: datacenter_id
      required: false
      type: string
    - description: 'Comma-separated port spec for the pod (default: ''8888/http,22/tcp'').'
      name: ports
      required: false
      type: string
    outputs:
    - name: pod_handle
      type: file
      path_template: '{out}/produces/pod_handle.json'
      mode: create_or_replace
      artifact_type: runpod/pod-handle
      description: Secret-safe durable pod handle for later exec, pull, or teardown.
    - name: cost
      type: file
      path_template: '{out}/produces/cost.json'
      mode: create_or_replace
      artifact_type: runpod/cost
      description: Local cost sidecar for the provision operation.
    resources:
    - kind: implementation
      path: actions/provision/__init__.py
    - kind: implementation
      path: actions/provision/run.py
    cache:
      mode: none
    conditions: []
    graph:
      consumes: []
      provides:
      - pod_handle
      - cost
    isolation:
      mode: subprocess
      network: true
      env_passthrough:
      - RUNPOD_SSH_IDENTITY_PUBLIC_PATH
      - RUNPOD_SSH_IDENTITY_PATH
      requirements:
      - runpod-lifecycle>=0.3.1.dev0,<0.4
    metadata:
      catalog_source: none_declared
      homepage: https://github.com/peteromallet/runpod-lifecycle
      manifest_only: true
      network_behavior:
        provision: true

        teardown: true

        - rest.runpod.io:443
        - graphql.runpod.io:443
        - runpod.io:443
        allow_redirects: false
        broker:

          kind: broker
          enforced: true
          observable: true
          route: declared-http-routes
          wrapper: astrid-generic-host
        descendant_enforcement:

schema_version: 3
id: wan2gp
name: Astrid Wan2GP
version: 1.0.0
status: active
domain: generation
stability: experimental
support: core
visibility: visible
permissions:
  - id: subprocess
    reason: Runs Wan2GP native Python engine (shared.api / WanGPSession) for video generation.
  - id: project_files
    reason: Reads input images/videos and writes generated outputs to private spool.
  - id: accelerator
    reason: May use GPU for Wan2GP model inference when available.
description: Native Wan2GP video generation through the GenericPackHost-owned shared.api session (official upstream API candidate f3f204e5). The host retains the native interpreter; Runtime owns task authority and attempt publication.
keywords:
  - wan2gp
  - wan
  - video
  - generation
  - gpu
capabilities:
  - generate_video
  - validate_settings

# @banodoco/timeline-composition

Scaffold (Sprint 4). The eventual home of:

- `HypeComposition.tsx` and the rest of the Remotion composition.
- `EFFECT_REGISTRY` / `TRANSITION_REGISTRY` dispatch.
- The stable theme public API.

Sprint 4 ships **only the scaffold** plus the `./theme-api` sub-path —
re-exports of `effects.types`, `lib/animations`, and `ThemeContext` from
the in-tree `tools/remotion/src/` location. Theme components migrate off
the deep relative imports onto `@banodoco/timeline-composition/theme-api`
via the codemod at `tools/scripts/codemod-theme-api-imports.ts`.

The actual composition extraction lands in Sprint 5 (Phase 4d).

## Build / test

```
cd packages/timeline-composition
npm install
npm run build
npm test
```

# Astrid local font provenance

These are the only font binaries used by the Remotion render. They are bundled
so an offline render never asks Google Fonts, a CDN, or another network host
for CSS or font bytes. `OFL-1.1.txt` is shipped beside these binaries and
contains the complete license text and copyright notices.

The upstream Google Fonts repository revision used for the Gelasio records
below is:

`ade3d1533e06b2b1462ffcde8e08b129627ca360`

Inter and JetBrains Mono were re-vendored from their upstream releases (the
Google Fonts copies they replace covered 2 of 95 printable ASCII characters;
see `LOCAL_FONT_ACCEPTANCE.md`).

Every family below is distributed under the SIL Open Font License, Version
1.1. The local binary SHA-256 values below are the acceptance-manifest values;
the upstream Git blob values identify the authoritative source record and are
not expected to equal a locally subsetted or format-converted binary.

## Sixtyfour

- Theme role: 2RP heading (`Sixtyfour`, variable BLED/SCAN axes).
- Local file: `Sixtyfour.woff2` (7,608 bytes).
- Local SHA-256: `0c35bb8333a12a822333f10fc4fd22e607b80a254b8b31faa8eed1cd4badc24e`.
- Upstream source: [homecomputer-fonts Sixtyfour webfont](https://github.com/jenskutilek/homecomputer-fonts/blob/22842dfb97fd3e7970383625cd3d10108edb8b5e/Sixtyfour/fonts/webfonts/Sixtyfour%5BBLED%2CSCAN%5D.woff2).
- Upstream revision: `22842dfb97fd3e7970383625cd3d10108edb8b5e`.
- Upstream Git blob: `368300391c703dcc22e6ea33fa9cff1cd377d385`.
- License: SIL Open Font License 1.1; copyright notice is `Copyright 2021 The Sixtyfour Project Authors (https://github.com/jenskutilek/homecomputer-fonts)`.
- Google Fonts curation record: `ofl/sixtyfour/` at the pinned Google Fonts revision above; its source TTF blob is `32985b4486ba627ad9b044be33b6d801b2d6d171`.

## Inter

- Theme role: 2RP body text.
- Local files: `Inter-Regular.woff2` (40,128 bytes, 400 upright), `Inter-Bold.woff2` (41,296 bytes, 700 upright). Static faces; they replace the earlier variable Google Fonts subsets.
- Local SHA-256: `5f04e9f02a74eab4ec87eda5b79b5be1c0567c868688b0a08564b2fe5c6da928` (regular); `aeaf0d0fa3262f4df2da7acf660544cb15aa24dcb63e574daed6ba7e92333a01` (bold).
- Upstream source: [rsms/inter release v4.1](https://github.com/rsms/inter/releases/tag/v4.1), asset `Inter-4.1.zip` (33,707,794 bytes, SHA-256 `9883fdd4a49d4fb66bd8177ba6625ef9a64aa45899767dde3d36aa425756b11e`). Members used: `extras/ttf/Inter-Regular.ttf` (411,640 bytes, SHA-256 `40d692fce188e4471e2b3cba937be967878f631ad3ebbbdcd587687c7ebe0c82`) and `extras/ttf/Inter-Bold.ttf` (420,428 bytes, SHA-256 `288316099b1e0a47a4716d159098005eef7c0066921f34e3200393dbdb01947f`).
- Upstream revision: tag `v4.1` at commit `e3a3d4c57d5ecc01453a575621882a384c1995a3`.
- Derivation: the official static TTFs are subset to the Latin set listed under Gelasio, plus the arrow block U+2190-2199, with all layout features kept and written as WOFF2 (`fontTools` 4.60.2, `brotli` 1.2.0). Result: 292 codepoints, 95/95 printable ASCII.
- Previous files (superseded, Google Fonts `ofl/inter` at ade3d15, variable `Inter[opsz,wght].ttf`): 27,380 and 19,980 bytes, SHA-256 `39689184...` and `47d42151...`. They covered 2 of 95 printable ASCII.
- License: SIL Open Font License 1.1; copyright notice is `Copyright (c) 2016 The Inter Project Authors (https://github.com/rsms/inter)`, as in the release `LICENSE.txt`.

## JetBrains Mono

- Theme role: 2RP monospace text.
- Local files: `JetBrainsMono-Regular.woff2` (35,416 bytes, 400 upright), `JetBrainsMono-Bold.woff2` (36,856 bytes, 700 upright). Static faces; they replace the earlier Google Fonts subsets.
- Local SHA-256: `2955337d809a64d58c56730b8344315198ec76214e02710774dd72d6a5de7b87` (regular); `a1475eef9934d6b3a6d15494f312ee1056b7556d59b1e22cb4e0c618338cd170` (bold).
- Upstream source: [JetBrains/JetBrainsMono release v2.304](https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono/releases/tag/v2.304), asset `JetBrainsMono-2.304.zip` (5,622,857 bytes, SHA-256 `6f6376c6ed2960ea8a963cd7387ec9d76e3f629125bc33d1fdcd7eb7012f7bbf`). Members used: `fonts/ttf/JetBrainsMono-Regular.ttf` (SHA-256 `a0bf60ef0f83c5ed4d7a75d45838548b1f6873372dfac88f71804491898d138f`) and `fonts/ttf/JetBrainsMono-Bold.ttf` (SHA-256 `5590990c82e097397517f275f430af4546e1c45cff408bde4255dad142479dcb`).
- Upstream revision: tag `v2.304` at commit `cd5227bd1f61dff3bbd6c814ceaf7ffd95e947d9`.
- Derivation: the same subset as Inter. Result: 249 codepoints, 95/95 printable ASCII. The upstream font has no U+2009 thin space, so that character is not in these faces and falls back.
- Previous files (superseded, Google Fonts `ofl/jetbrainsmono` at ade3d15): 2,180 and 13,352 bytes, SHA-256 `1b535365...` and `8df3ca62...`. They covered 2 of 95 printable ASCII.
- License: SIL Open Font License 1.1; copyright notice is `Copyright 2020 The JetBrains Mono Project Authors (https://github.com/JetBrains/JetBrainsMono)`, as in the release `OFL.txt`.

## Departure Mono

- Theme role: Astrid video label face (pixel monospace, `production/STYLE.md`); family name `Departure Mono`.
- Local file: `DepartureMono-Regular.woff2` (22,496 bytes), copied byte-for-byte from the upstream release; no subsetting or conversion.
- Local SHA-256: `5b4fed1daa90708aa9c6ee1190abca9dc22164a1c1def0020386e46b61038cfb`. This is identical to the astrid.haus copy at `production/references/site/raw/DepartureMono-Regular.woff2`.
- Upstream source: [rektdeckard/departure-mono release v1.500](https://github.com/rektdeckard/departure-mono/releases/tag/v1.500), asset `DepartureMono-1.500.zip` (82,890 bytes, SHA-256 `bf3e48059aeef4617ec585bdea81dcc3491c576b3e7a472f52faf40e09ee5c3a`), member `DepartureMono-1.500/DepartureMono-Regular.woff2`.
- Upstream revision: tag `v1.500` at commit `75152a3f1e6dacdd248a6c397c97dbf27e33eea0` (released 2025-05-25). The woff2 has 1,079 codepoints and covers all 95 printable ASCII characters.
- Author: Helena Zhang.
- License: SIL Open Font License 1.1; copyright notice is `Copyright 2022–2024 Helena Zhang (helenazhang.com)`. The license text is the release archive's `LICENSE` file (reproduced in `OFL-1.1.txt`), and the font's name table records the OFL in nameID 13. The repository's root `LICENSE` file is MIT; it is not the license of the font binary and is not relied on here.

## Gelasio

- Theme role: Astrid video headline serif, a metric-compatible stand-in for Georgia (`production/STYLE.md` names Georgia as the display face and Georgia is a system font that the renderer does not load). Designer: Eben Sorkin.
- Local files: `Gelasio-Regular.woff2` (20,284 bytes, 400 upright), `Gelasio-Italic.woff2` (22,272 bytes, 400 italic), `Gelasio-Bold.woff2` (20,452 bytes, 700 upright), `Gelasio-BoldItalic.woff2` (22,476 bytes, 700 italic).
- Local SHA-256: `698c2aa61ec1960371b6ed32e6120f028fa614613256f4b9e3f5d10ceb013eb5` (regular); `2df3d4a4d0cefc6440710666fa425627e54cb73707224bec044bca8e65940222` (italic); `2fdaa469d51ef618d648e27819f10a1df08721ed2331614c3123850162cc147a` (bold); `e5b0682ff74c6798100255daafaf5d5496c5ddec596aec663fdd0afb3470b609` (bold italic).
- Upstream family: [Google Fonts `ofl/gelasio`](https://github.com/google/fonts/tree/ade3d1533e06b2b1462ffcde8e08b129627ca360/ofl/gelasio), whose variable sources are `Gelasio[wght].ttf` (168,556 bytes, SHA-256 `4daecea457258c9ebeb8bc99ed3fd24353618bfad3ea4b93fa0b5d0468fc04e4`, Git blob `23711d2fa49ab8c60301f8fd718cc10614db693a`) and `Gelasio-Italic[wght].ttf` (174,212 bytes, SHA-256 `52559e845a4d33514e5f93bb9ae7dbeae1894a53f2c565a15f18af40cd337c09`, Git blob `21e3c87ca4dbf1e298a0b4ce5e31e1fbeb0e7ea4`).
- Upstream revision: `ade3d1533e06b2b1462ffcde8e08b129627ca360` (Google Fonts). The upstream repository is [SorkinType/Gelasio](https://github.com/SorkinType/Gelasio) at commit `9228e69b160d79f33950e026293f6e13ba9780d0`; both variable TTFs there (`fonts/variable/`) are byte-identical to the Google Fonts files above (SHA-256 checked).
- Derivation: the static faces are instances of the variable TTFs at `wght=400` and `wght=700` (`fontTools` 4.60.2 `varLib.instancer --update-name-table`), then subset to the Google Fonts `latin` range (`U+0000-00FF, U+0131, U+0152-0153, U+02BB-02BC, U+02C6, U+02DA, U+02DC, U+0304, U+0308, U+0329, U+2000-206F, U+20AC, U+2122, U+2191, U+2193, U+2212, U+2215, U+FEFF, U+FFFD`) with all layout features kept, and written as WOFF2 (`brotli` 1.2.0). The subset contains 250 codepoints, including every character of the glyph probe.
- License: SIL Open Font License 1.1 (`License: SIL Open Font License 1.1`, Google Fonts `METADATA.pb` `license: "OFL"`); copyright notice is `Copyright 2022 The Gelasio Project Authors (https://github.com/SorkinType/Gelasio)`. The Google Fonts `OFL.txt` has the same license body as `OFL-1.1.txt` with different line wrapping (SHA-256 of that file `b393cb01867c919b44381512120dc3e4c954c7b47e2035c405f3a324799a4d29`).

## Acceptance contract

`src/fonts.ts` must remain the sole source of the local `@font-face` rules.
Every family named by the 2RP theme or the Astrid video brand must have a local
face in that list. The loader waits for `document.fonts.load` and verifies
`document.fonts.check` for each family/style/weight; any missing face cancels
the Remotion render. Faces with `style: "italic"` load with the `italic` font
keyword. The focused test also rejects hosted font imports, URL fetches, and
missing glyph-proof coverage.

Every shipped face must cover all 95 printable ASCII characters (U+0020-U+007E).
The loader's `document.fonts.check` probe cannot detect a missing glyph (the
browser falls through to the next family silently), so coverage is pinned in
`tests/fixtures/remotion-font-coverage.json`: per face, the SHA-256, the cmap
size and the list of missing printable ASCII. The test fails on any binary
change until the record is regenerated, on any unrecorded `.woff2`, and on any
missing ASCII. When `fontTools` and `brotli` are importable, the test also
recomputes the cmap from the binaries. To regenerate after a change:

```python
from fontTools.ttLib import TTFont
import hashlib, json, pathlib
fonts = pathlib.Path("remotion/public/fonts")
out = {"description": "Printable ASCII (U+0020-U+007E) coverage per shipped Remotion font face, generated with fontTools from the committed woff2 files.", "ascii_range": "U+0020-U+007E", "files": {}}
for path in sorted(fonts.glob("*.woff2")):
    cmap = TTFont(path).getBestCmap()
    missing = [chr(c) for c in range(0x20, 0x7F) if c not in cmap]
    out["files"][path.name] = {"sha256": hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                               "cmap_codepoints": len(cmap),
                               "ascii_covered": 95 - len(missing), "ascii_missing": missing}
with open("tests/fixtures/remotion-font-coverage.json", "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
    json.dump(out, fh, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False)
    fh.write("\n")
```

Receipt date: 2026-08-30

The acceptance probe is committed at
`tests/fixtures/remotion-local-font-probe.json`. It renders the exact glyph
probe `Astrid 2RP — Aa 0123` through the Sixtyfour heading family while the
loader simultaneously waits for and checks Sixtyfour, Inter, and JetBrains
Mono. The probe uses no media assets, so a successful non-black text frame is
font evidence rather than an incidental source image.

## Checks

- `python3 -m pytest -q tests/test_remotion_local_fonts.py` — PASS (4 tests).
- `npm run typecheck` — PASS.
- `npm run bundle` — PASS.
- `sandbox-exec -p '(version 1) (allow default) (deny network-outbound) (allow network-outbound (remote ip "localhost:*"))' ./node_modules/.bin/remotion render src/index.ts TimelineComposition /tmp/astrid-local-font-offline.mp4 --props ../tests/fixtures/remotion-local-font-probe.json --frames=0-29 --log=verbose` — PASS (exit 0; committed network-denial receipt below).
- Offline render receipt: H.264/AAC, 1920×1080, 30 frames, 1.045333 seconds; output SHA-256 `64af64f4d9076375eb1339fcb15cce5f6da6587c217d403c6e0119ad3c058f28`.
- Frame-15 visual evidence SHA-256 `ef0b5418d465bdfaddfcf3765e7fe1bd225120d4b2f1c86d300d8453f722f05e` (Sixtyfour, Inter, and JetBrains Mono rows all visibly rendered).
- Verbose output recorded five `Loading Astrid local fonts` completions and zero Google-font host markers. The full filtered receipt is `LOCAL_FONT_NETWORK_DENY.log`.

## Offline contract

The focused test rejects `@remotion/google-fonts`, Google Fonts hosts,
`fetch()`, and `XMLHttpRequest` in the loader. The runtime loader constructs
all sources from Remotion `staticFile()` paths, passes the committed glyph
probe to `document.fonts.load()` and `document.fonts.check()`, and invokes
`cancelRender()` on any missing face. This is the fail-closed path: offline
failure cannot silently become a system-font or hosted-font fallback.

The repository's broader `npm run smoke` remains a known pre-existing failure
because its generated-types snapshot omits `derivedFrom`, `media_id`, and
`origin` while the generated source exports them; this font change does not
touch that snapshot or alter the failure.

## Re-vendor of Inter and JetBrains Mono (2026-10-09)

Why: the Inter and JetBrains Mono faces shipped since 2026-08-30 cover almost
no printable ASCII. Lowercase letters, digits and most punctuation were absent
from the cmap, so the browser silently drew them in the next family of the
stack. The loader cannot see this: `document.fonts.check` reports a loaded face
as ready regardless of its cmap, and the frame-15 visual evidence above cannot
tell a shipped face from a system fallback. The Sixtyfour, Departure Mono and
Gelasio faces already cover all 95 printable ASCII characters.

What changed: Inter 400/700 and JetBrains Mono 400/700 are now static faces
made from the official upstream releases, not the variable Google Fonts
subsets. Sources and hashes are in `FONT_PROVENANCE.md`. The subset uses the
Latin set of the Gelasio derivation plus the arrow block U+2190-2199. Filenames
and the `LOCAL_FONT_FACES` entries are unchanged.

Coverage (cmap codepoints; printable ASCII out of 95; label extras out of 17,
which are U+00B7 · U+00D7 × U+2212 − U+2192 → U+2190 ← U+2191 ↑ U+2193 ↓
U+2014 — U+2013 – U+2018 ‘ U+2019 ’ U+201C “ U+201D ” U+2026 … U+2009 thin
space U+00B0 ° U+00E9 é):

| Face | Before: cmap / ASCII / extras / bytes / fvar | After: cmap / ASCII / extras / bytes / fvar |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Inter-Regular | 157 / 2 / 0 / 27,380 / yes | 292 / 95 / 17 / 40,128 / no |
| Inter-Bold | 107 / 2 / 0 / 19,980 / yes | 292 / 95 / 17 / 41,296 / no |
| JetBrainsMono-Regular | 10 / 2 / 0 / 2,180 / yes | 249 / 95 / 16 / 35,416 / no |
| JetBrainsMono-Bold | 102 / 2 / 0 / 13,352 / yes | 249 / 95 / 16 / 36,856 / no |

Known gap, not fixed: the upstream JetBrains Mono has no U+2009 thin space, so
that character falls back in the JetBrains Mono faces. Gelasio's Google Fonts
latin subset has no U+2190 or U+2192 arrows. Neither gap affects printable
ASCII, which is what the regression test enforces.

Checks run (2026-10-09): `tests/test_remotion_local_fonts.py` passes, 6 of 6,
including every shipped face's printable ASCII coverage against
`tests/fixtures/remotion-font-coverage.json`, a recomputation from the binaries
with `fontTools` (present in the venv), and the byte/hash manifest. Negative
controls: swapping in the old Inter binary, a record that reports `a` missing,
and an unrecorded extra `.woff2` each make the test fail. Visual check: a PIL
render of the shipped woff2 files shows the new glyphs (PIL draws the old
binaries as missing-glyph boxes; a browser would show the system fallback).

Not re-run: the offline Remotion render above (output hash `64af64f4...`,
frame-15 hash `ef0b5418...`) was produced with the old Inter and JetBrains Mono
binaries and no longer describes the shipped faces. The re-render needs the
Remotion install (Node 20.19.4, `remotion/node_modules`) and is pending. Until
it is re-run, the render evidence for these two families is missing.

# @banodoco/timeline-theme-2rp

First peer-dep theme package for `@banodoco/timeline-composition`. Sprint 5
deliverable. Ships:

- `theme.json` — theme metadata (color, type, motion, canvas).
- `src/effects/<clipType>/component.tsx` — Remotion components for
  `section-hook`, `art-card`, `cta-card`, `resource-card`.
- `src/effects/<clipType>/{schema,defaults,meta}.json` — per-effect
  schema/defaults/meta companions (mirror the Banodoco in-tree shape).

## Install

```sh
npm install @banodoco/timeline-theme-2rp
```

The package resolves to a `file:` link in this monorepo / convergence
workspace; no npm publishing happens this sprint.

## Discovery

`@banodoco/timeline-composition`'s `gen-registry.ts` codegen walks
`node_modules/@banodoco/timeline-theme-*` and emits one entry per
`src/effects/<clipType>/component.tsx`. After install, run
`npm run gen-registry` in the composition package (or rely on the CI
shim's pre-test hook).

## Notes

- The original `themes/2rp/` directory remains under banodoco-workspace
  for `tools/effects_catalog.py` discovery (which still scans the in-tree
  path during Banodoco CLI render). Sprint 5 intentionally duplicates
  the components into this peer-dep package; de-duplication is a
  follow-on (point `effects_catalog.py` at `packages/timeline-theme-*/`).
